result:
I found and fixed 11 rules in `pricebook.py` whose behavior didn't match their docstrings. After the fixes, a check script compared all 150 rules against what their docstrings say, over a range of quantities and unit prices, and found no mismatches.

| Rule | Original code | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 07 | marginal rule computed the discount on the whole amount | discount on units above 30 only (`(qty - 30) * unit`) |
| 14 | 13% discount | 12% |
| 32 | marginal rule computed the discount on the whole amount | discount on units above 100 only (`(qty - 100) * unit`) |
| 39 | capped the price before applying the rate | applies 7% first, then caps the discount at 100,000 won |
| 47 | whole rule computed the discount only on units above the threshold | discount on the whole amount (`base`) |
| 56 | threshold was `qty >= 6` | `qty >= 5` |
| 72 | cap applied only when the discount exceeded 20,000 won (discounts between 10,000 and 20,000 slipped through) | always capped at 10,000 won |
| 85 | `round()` rounded to the nearest won | floored with `// 100` |
| 90 | `round()` rounded to the nearest won | floored with `// 100` |
| 131 | 16% discount | 15% |
| 140 | marginal rule computed the discount on the whole amount | discount on units above 50 only (`(qty - 50) * unit`) |

A few rules are written differently from the rest but give the same results, so I left them alone:
- Rules 28, 49, 66, 95, 125, 127 and 148 use forms like `if not qty < N`, `(qty * unit)` or `if disc > cap:`.
- Rule 121 uses `qty > 5` instead of `qty >= 5`. That gives the same price because at 5 units there are no units above the threshold, so the discount is 0 either way.

The check covered boundary quantities around each threshold and also confirmed that negative input raises `ValueError`.

STATUS: DONE
